requirement_text: TOEFL iBT and TOEFL iBT Home Edition: 1 - 6 score scale taken from 21st January 2026
limitations: This row names the SCALE and its date boundary; the per-band numeric thresholds sit on a separate QMUL page that did not surface them (see REQ-9207 to REQ-9209, which carry IELTS bands only). Not a threshold on its own.
researcher_notes: BEST-IN-CORPUS HANDLING of the ETS rescale. QMUL is the only source found that names the scale explicitly ('1 - 6 score scale') rather than leaving it inferable from the numbers, and gives both sides of the boundary to the day. Every other institution either dates the rows without naming the scale (Bath, Exeter, ITU) or does neither (Manchester, Glasgow, Bogazici). If ORYN ever needs a reference implementation of test_scale, this is it.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT and TOEFL iBT Home Edition: 0-120 score scale taken up to 20th January 2026
limitations: Note the boundary is stated as 'up to 20th January 2026', i.e. exclusive of the 21st, which is the exact complement of REQ-9201. No overlap and no gap. Becomes unusable in January 2028 when ETS ends comparable 0-120 reporting, at which point this row should be retired rather than reinterpreted.
researcher_notes: Paired with REQ-9201. Together they are the only complete, gapless two-sided scale definition found in this corpus.

limitations: Listed by QMUL among tests and score types it does not accept. requirement_text is the item as named on the page; the surrounding 'not accepted' framing is carried by is_exclusion rather than being spliced into the quotation.
researcher_notes: EXCLUSION ON SCORE PROVENANCE. Second institution after Edinburgh to name MyBest specifically. A MyBest composite and a single-sitting total can be the same number, and a threshold comparison answers met for both. Confirms the provenance-flag recommendation in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md section 3 is not an Edinburgh idiosyncrasy.

limitations: Named among the tests QMUL does not accept. The exclusion framing is carried by is_exclusion, not spliced into the quotation.
researcher_notes: EXCLUSION ON TEST VARIANT. IELTS General and IELTS Academic report on the same 0-9 band scale, so a student's stored 'IELTS 7.0' is indistinguishable between them unless the variant is stored alongside the number. ORYN's test_scores table would answer met for a General 7.0 that QMUL rejects outright.

limitations: Named among tests QMUL does not accept. Exclusion framing carried by is_exclusion.
researcher_notes: EXCLUSION ON DELIVERY MODE, and note QMUL DOES accept TOEFL iBT Home Edition (REQ-9201) and IELTS Online. So within one institution the online/in-centre rule differs by test - the same per-test inconsistency found at Bath. Delivery mode cannot be modelled as an institution-level flag anywhere.

requirement_text: This test should have been achieved no more than 2 years from the start date of your course
limitations: RECENCY RULE, anchored to 'the start date of your course'. Applies to the standardized tests; QMUL gives school qualifications a longer window (5-7 years), so this is another per-qualification-type split.
researcher_notes: Fifth institution in the corpus with a recency rule and the third distinct anchor phrasing. Anchors seen so far: 'prior to entry' (Edinburgh), 'starting your course' (Bath), 'the first day of your course' (Liverpool), 'the start date of your course' (QMUL, Southampton). They plausibly mean the same instant, but a max-age constraint that does not record which phrasing it came from cannot be audited later.

requirement_text: IELTS (Academic) minimum score 6.0 overall with 5.5 in each of Writing, Listening, Reading and Speaking
limitations: Subject to the REQ-9204 exclusion (IELTS General not accepted) and the REQ-9206 recency rule. Neither is visible from this row alone.
researcher_notes: Band 3 applies to the School of Electronic Engineering and Computer Science; School of Engineering and Materials Science; School of Mathematical Sciences; School of Physical and Chemical Sciences; School of Biological and Behavioural Sciences. This school-to-band mapping is the reusable structure: one row covers every programme in five schools, which is the cheapest coverage of any record in this batch.

requirement_text: IELTS (Academic) minimum score 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each of Writing, Listening, Reading and Speaking
limitations: Subject to the REQ-9204 exclusion and the REQ-9206 recency rule.
researcher_notes: Band 4 applies to the School of Business and Management; School of Economics and Finance; School of Society and Environment. Economics and Finance is directly relevant to ORYN's stated example persona.

requirement_text: IELTS (Academic) minimum score 7.0 overall with 6.0 in each of Writing, Listening, Reading and Speaking
limitations: Subject to the REQ-9204 exclusion and the REQ-9206 recency rule. Note the per-section floor does NOT rise in step with the overall between Band 4 and Band 5 - both require 6.0 per section. A scoring rule that derives section floors from the overall band would be wrong here.
researcher_notes: Band 5 applies to the School of the Arts; Blizard Institute; Institute of Dentistry; Institute of Health Sciences Education.

requirement_text: Each course has its own English language proficiency requirement, expressed as an English language band (A to I) and its International English Language Testing System (IELTS) equivalent.
limitations: STRUCTURE, NOT A THRESHOLD. Southampton publishes nine bands (A to I) and the per-band numbers live in a separate per-entry-year PDF that could not be extracted (see the blocked list). Recorded so the next lane knows the shape it is looking for and does not mistake a single course's IELTS score for a university-wide rule.
researcher_notes: Third distinct banding vocabulary in this batch alone - Bath uses lettered categories A/B/C, QMUL numbered bands 3/4/5, Southampton letters A to I, Exeter named profiles B2/B3/E/F. Four incompatible schemes across four UK universities. Any attempt to normalise 'band' across institutions will silently merge unrelated things; the band label is only meaningful paired with its institution.

requirement_text: (IELTS) Academic UKVI SELT (including One Skill Retake)
researcher_notes: DIRECT INVERSION of an existing corpus record. Edinburgh states 'We do not accept IELTS One Skill Retake to meet our English language requirements'; Southampton names One Skill Retake as accepted, in parentheses, inside its list of approved tests. Two UK universities, same test variant, opposite answers, both official and both current. This is the strongest available evidence that score PROVENANCE has to be stored per institution and cannot be a global property of the test, and it is a case where a student's honest answer to 'does my score count?' is different at two universities on the same UCAS form.

limitations: Named in Southampton's Cambridge-qualifications list with the disposition 'Not accepted'. The disposition is carried by is_exclusion rather than spliced into the quotation.
researcher_notes: EXCLUSION matching Manchester's REQ-9009 ('English as a Second Language' not accepted). Two of the seven UK institutions in this batch specifically exclude the second-language IGCSE English variant, which is the one most commonly held by exactly the international students ORYN targets. Worth surfacing to students proactively rather than at requirement-check time.

limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary: the extraction returned this sentence with an internal elision, so the wording between 'must be' and 'awarded' is not recovered. The 2-year window and the course-start-date anchor are reliable; the exact sentence is not. Re-read before displaying.
researcher_notes: RECENCY RULE. Sixth institution with one. Marked NEEDS_REVIEW on fidelity grounds rather than on substance - the fact is sound, the quotation is not.
